title: Stationarity, ACF & PACF
interviewAnswer: Stationarity means the statistical behavior of a series is stable enough over time for many classical models to learn consistent relationships. I inspect trend/seasonality and autocorrelation; differencing or transformation can help when the level is non-stationary.
why: ARIMA-family methods rely on structure in lagged values and residuals. Understanding autocorrelation also helps diagnose leakage and seasonality.
intuition: ACF asks “how correlated is the series with itself k steps ago?” PACF tries to isolate the direct lag-k relationship after accounting for shorter lags.
deepDive: Weak stationarity is typically about approximately constant mean/variance and covariance depending on lag rather than absolute time. ACF/PACF are diagnostics, not magical parameter selectors. Differencing can remove stochastic trends but over-differencing adds noise.
workedExample: A monthly series with a rising level may show slow ACF decay. First differencing y_t-y_{t-1} can make the remaining dependence easier to model; a spike at lag 12 can suggest annual seasonality.
commonMistakes: Blindly differencing until a statistical test passes without checking business meaning.
followUps: What does an ACF spike at a seasonal lag mean?
production: Monitor residual autocorrelation after deployment; systematic temporal structure in errors often means the model is leaving forecastable signal unused.
math: ACF(k) = Corr(y_t, y_{t-k}).  First difference: Δy_t = y_t - y_{t-1}.

visual.title: Autocorrelation by lag
visual.caption: The ACF summarizes correlation between a series and lagged versions of itself; slow decay can signal persistent structure.
